correctness.rationale: Parity forces the left quotient D to be in G. If the group coordinates of the bracketings are P and Q, the quotient is P Q^-1 for even parity and Q^-1 P for odd parity, by the four multiplication rules. Expanding gives the displayed commutators in sectors 001, 010, 100, 011, 101 and 110; each fixes a free third variable and changes the other two bijectively to a commutator pair. For example, 101 uses u=c^-1 a and [u^-1,b]. In 111 the resulting commutator can be written [b^-1 c,b^-1 a] by conjugating both arguments, so fixing b again gives a bijective parametrization. Thus the seven sector counts are n C_G(g) and 000 contributes n^3 only at identity. Normalization by 8n^3 and the classical Frobenius formula give the character expression, which is unchanged under g -> g^-1. Sector 001 realizes every commutator, and the subgroup they generate inside G is precisely the associative subloop [G,G]. The symbolic proof applies also in the trivial and abelian cases; the supplied examples are not needed for generality.
